renderer.note: Vendored directly rather than as a submodule. Only the Rust crates, the C++ scene engine and their build files remain here. 2026-09-16: crates/bridge routes `type: "web"` projects away from the scene engine — WallpaperEntry marks Web supported, ProjectModel parses `file`, ActivationInputs takes project models and splits build() (engine scenes) from build_web() (WebWallpaperDesc per assigned/mirrored display), active ids include configured web wallpapers, and the uniffi surface gains `web_wallpapers()` returning BridgeWebWallpaper for the Swift-hosted WKWebView windows. Local 2026-09-17 playback changes publish committed native pointer capability through a bounded renderer-instance relay, serialize consumer activation with the shared button tracker, gate the existing poller by consumers and pause policy, batch samples in one actor turn, and deduplicate only successful identical position/enter writes. Level-only native button reconciliation preserves held levels across video gating. These internal runtime changes do not alter the persisted or UniFFI schema. Local 2026-09-17 power work makes presentation suspension per display: BridgeActorState keeps suspended_displays beside the global presentation_suspended flag, ActivationInputs resolves each scene's and web descriptor's paused state from its own display (mirrors included), EngineFacade gains set_display_paused, a global resume re-applies the displays that are still hidden, and the new uniffi method set_display_presentation_suspended carries one display's decision without touching the others or the user's Play/Pause choice. System audio capture is gated on visible consumers — a scene that is presenting and has audio response enabled — so hiding every audio wallpaper stops the analysis while volume and mute stay independent controls; mouse polling follows whether any display still presents. Covered by crates/bridge/src/tests/display_presentation.rs. 2026-09-17 (second round): wallpaper-core exposes render::RendererSurfaceCounters and WallpaperEngine::renderer_counters/set_renderer_counters_enabled over the new OWE counter ABI; crates/bridge adds the uniffi set_renderer_counters_enabled and renderer_counters returning BridgeRendererCountersReport, which keeps surface-exclusive work and shared source work apart and reports presentation feedback as unavailable rather than approximating it with present requests. 2026-09-18 (third round): crates/bridge gains the experimental native video routing — AppConfig.experimental.native_video_backend, ActivationInputs::build_native_video producing NativeVideoWallpaperDesc, build() excluding those ids so no scene is created for them, and the uniffi set_native_video_backend_enabled / native_video_wallpapers / reject_native_video. A host refusal is recorded once per wallpaper for the session, so the two backends cannot pass a wallpaper back and forth. Counters gained OWE_RC_VIDEO_SOURCE_COUNT and OWE_RC_VIDEO_SOURCE_INSTANCE so source work is attributed to a running decoder instance rather than to a file path. 2026-09-18: trimmed to what this repository builds — removed upstream's README and README screenshots (assets/), GitHub workflows, Nix flake/dev shell (nix/, flake.nix, flake.lock, .envrc) and the stale .gitmodules; crates/core/build.rs no longer passes BUILD_WAYWALLEN/BUILD_QML. LICENSE is retained; restore removed files from the pinned revision if needed. 2026-09-18 (V04): native-video refusals are keyed by an admission key instead of by wallpaper id alone. NativeVideoWallpaperDesc and BridgeNativeVideoWallpaper carry `admission_key`, an FNV-1a hash over the resolved media path, the media file's length and modification time, and the display's effective target fps, computed in ActivationInputs::build_native_video; RejectNativeVideo takes that key back and drops a refusal whose key no longer matches the live configuration, so a refusal that lost a race with the user cannot kill the configuration that replaced it. BridgeActorState::native_video_rejected became BTreeMap<String, NativeVideoRejection>, activation ignores a record whose key differs, and the map is pruned when the host next asks what to play. Raising the target rate, restoring a setting or replacing the media file at the same path therefore re-offers the wallpaper; clear-on-toggle is unchanged and the backend is still off by default. Counters gained VideoConversionLiveBytes and VideoConversionPeakLiveBytes in crates/core/src/render/counters.rs, and BridgeRendererSurfaceCounters gained video_conversion_live_bytes and video_conversion_peak_live_bytes, so the bytes a surface's video conversion destinations occupy are readable from a diagnostic report without a gtest. Both are allocation gauges over those destination textures only — decode CVPixelBuffers, Core Video plane wrappers, the Vulkan images aliasing them and the swapchain are excluded — and neither is a claim about physical residency or process footprint. A follow-up keyed those refusals per (wallpaper id, admission key) rather than per wallpaper id: a wallpaper has one admission key per display slot, and the single-record store let a second display's refusal overwrite the first's, after which the first display's record looked stale, was pruned, and the clip was offered natively again to a host that had already refused that exact key — leaving that display with no backend at all. Local 2026-09-18 round 5 adds three user-operable features. R01 internal render scale: Scene gains a latched authored `scene_extent` and a `render_scale`, SceneRenderTarget gains `authored_width`/`authored_height` and a `media_sized` flag, PassCommon resolves the authored canvas and the internal raster separately so presentation layout and cursor mapping stay on the authored size, VulkanRender::ApplyRenderScale re-prepares passes in place through a new TextureCache::ClearRenderTargets that keeps uploaded images and live decoders, and `owe_scene_wallpaper_set_render_scale` exposes it. D01 shared video decode: new Video/SharedVideoSession keyed on canonical path plus size and mtime, per-consumer handles with independently retained frames via a new VideoTextureSource::retainCurrentFrame and RetainAppleVideoFrame, a file-path FfmpegVideoTextureSource constructor for splitting an incompatible consumer onto its own decoder, and `owe_set_shared_video_decode_enabled` plus session/consumer counts. Content pacing becomes a process-wide setting (`owe_set_content_pacing_enabled`) still seeded by MAC_WALLPAPER_ENGINE_CONTENT_PACING and still default off. crates/bridge gains AppConfig.video_backend with migration from the legacy experimental.native_video_backend key, a quality section with a battery profile, and the matching uniffi setters and snapshot fields. New tests: render_scale_test, shared_video_session_test, and tests/synthetic_video.hpp extracted from video_source_input_test. Local 2026-09-18 round 6 changes are threefold. R03 scene optimisation: Scene/VulkanRender gains StaticSubgraphCache and CopyElision, which reuse a render target's previous pixels when every writer's sampled inputs are unchanged and remove copy passes that have no consumer or that duplicate an image nothing rewrites; CustomShaderPass gains staticPassDesc/frameSample/setFrameSkipped, CopyPass gains an elision mode, TextureCache gains PinRenderTarget/AliasRenderTarget/RenderTargetBytes, IShaderValueUpdater gains FrameVaryingUniforms so staticness comes from captured shader reflection rather than shader source text, and SceneWallpaperBindings exposes owe_set_scene_optimization_enabled/owe_scene_optimization_enabled/owe_scene_optimization_stats. Audio: the CoreAudio tap is now stereo with an observable mono fallback, the resampler keeps both channels, AudioResponseService analyses two independent FFTs, AudioSpectrumSnapshot gains `stereo`, and owe_audio_spectrum_is_stereo reports it; submit_mono_audio_frames became a required trait method so no default can duplicate mono into fake stereo. crates/core gains AudioSpectrum128 plus WallpaperEngine::set_scene_optimization_enabled and current_audio_spectrum. crates/bridge gains file/directory/texture property kinds with filter and mode metadata, per-wallpaper media integration, web pages as audio-capture consumers, a verbatim media replay store, and the scene optimisation setting. Local 2026-09-19 (round 7) adds whole-scene on-demand updating and a first native Metal scene backend. On-demand: ThreadTimer gains a true idle wait with no deadline plus a latched WakeOnce/WakeAt, FrameTimer::FrameDemand gains Idle/Timed kinds, SceneRuntimeContext::DescribeTimeAdvancingWork reports which Tick facilities advance with time, VulkanRender publishes ShaderUpdateDemandReasons from reflection it already captured, and SceneWallpaper combines them into a SceneUpdateDemand; every non-draw render command and pointer input request one frame. Default off via owe_set_scene_on_demand_enabled. Metal: new src/Scene/MetalRender/ (ObjC++) draws 2D image layers with the author's own shaders translated to MSL by crates/shader's new metal_msl naga target; EvaluateMetalSupport gates whole scenes and SelectSceneBackend routes, with SceneRendererHandle owning exactly one backend so a CAMetalLayer never carries both a Vulkan swapchain and a Metal drawable. WPSceneParser gains a preference-gated second translation pass on copies, so the compatibility path is unchanged. Presentation/WallpaperScaling.cpp moved into wpVulkanRender and ApplyCameraFillMode was extracted into PassCommon.hpp so both backends share one definition. Default Compatibility via owe_set_scene_renderer_preference. 2026-09-19 (round 8): crates/bridge gains only a test (tests/scene_settings.rs: a scene with no backend yet is reported apart from a fallback); no bridge type, UniFFI schema or persisted setting changed. The scene-engine side of the round is listed in the sceneEngine note. 2026-09-19 (round 9): no Rust crate, UniFFI schema or persisted setting changed; the round is entirely in the C++ scene engine and is listed in the sceneEngine note.

sceneEngine.note: Property-script updates continue from the current dynamic value rather than restarting from the authored base each frame, preserving hover interpolation and explicit property writes. Script input serialization copies no live subscriptions. Synthetic regressions cover convergence, interrupted reversal and user-value replacement. Scene parsing, the scene runtime and the offscreen probes carry local fixes. Latest on 2026-09-16: property scripts bound to a layer's visible/origin/scale/angles settings are no longer dropped when the authored visible value is falsy; alignment anchors for image layers are owned by SceneRuntimeContext, and RegisterNode no longer re-seeds a registered anchor from the already-offset node translate, so a dynamic origin or scale can neither lose the anchor nor double-count it; offscreen_scene_probe requests the production device extensions and dumps node transforms. Also 2026-09-16: WPPuppetLayer copies share one playback state that SceneScript reaches as IAnimationLayer through SceneRuntimeContext::PuppetAnimationControl, with animationlayers visible/rate/blend bound to user properties; cursor hit tests run in layer-local space and consult a parse-time alpha coverage mask for cursor-scripted image layers; offscreen_scene_probe gains WE_TEST_CLICK_OFFSET. Also 2026-09-16: cursor input is mapped through the presented scaling viewport and global camera instead of the raw canvas, and named layers only receive cursor events inside the drawn content rectangle, so hit testing matches where cropped or letterboxed wallpapers actually draw; synthetic regressions cover the cropped-presentation hit test and letterbox rejection. Local 2026-09-17 playback changes repair shader/transfer/overwrite synchronization and propagate VkResult recording failures, share checked color-framebuffer caching, remove only proven redundant pre-clears, and add strictly bounded single-pass UNORM direct presentation while retaining the normal pipeline and all completion waits. Native scene commits publish pointer capability with transactional callback ownership and level-only button reconciliation. Compiled script export metadata preserves initialization, timers, live writeback and cursor semantics; generation-based material conversion and derived transform caches still repair destinations, and failed node registration restores masks/shared puppet state while releasing new subscriptions. Pose results now belong to the existing shared playback State, audio uniform packing reuses an owning buffer with fresh per-call snapshots, and particle mouse inverses are skipped only without current linked controlpoints. Also 2026-09-17: vector material constants resolve one curve per component and share the playback of the timeline named by `options.parent`, so a paused page-fold corner applies its authored first key instead of the static value, components without a curve keep their own value, and a missing or cyclic parent freezes that group on frame 0 after one logged error; offscreen_scene_probe's WE_TEST_DUMP_PASSES now dumps only the last sampled frame and appends each dumped pass's material slot constants to passes.txt, and tests/CMakeLists.txt links nlohmann_json into media_thumbnail_texture_smoke so that target builds. Follow-ups the same day: a material constant reaches its property script at the component count the shader declares (one as a float, two and four through the new ResolveVectorSetting, three unchanged), so a scripted vec2 corner is no longer handed over as text and returned as NaN; and authored timeline events are carried through ScalarAnimation::events, recorded by ScalarAnimationPlayback::Advance as the playhead crosses them (once per event for a stall longer than a loop, never on a seek) and drained each Tick — after the scripted values are re-evaluated, so a marker crossed by the first tick reaches an initialized handler — into the animationEvent export of the property and scene scripts bound to that layer, carrying the authored name and frame; the global engine.on list is run once per marker by the runtime, which also refreshes the engine object for it, rather than once per matching scene program. scene.getAnimation(name) is new: a null layer passed to __animationControl matches an authored name across every registered timeline. offscreen_scene_probe's dumped pass lines also record live visibility. Local 2026-09-17 power work adds src/Video/VideoDecodePump.{hpp,cpp}: a codec-agnostic, receive-first decode state machine (Reading/PacketHeld/Draining/Stopped/Failed) that resubmits a packet the decoder rejected with EAGAIN instead of releasing it, sends exactly one drain request per end of input and restarts the stream only after the decoder itself reports end of stream, polls cooperative cancellation between steps, bounds consecutive no-progress steps, and releases a held packet exactly once on seek, stop or failure. FfmpegVideoTextureSource drives it through a libavformat/libavcodec adapter, allocates its format context so an AVIOInterruptCB can abort a stalled read, publishes cancellation through an atomic flag, and distinguishes cancellation from failure so stopping records no error. src/Video/VideoColorConversion.{hpp,cpp} is the shared CPU/GPU colour contract: limited-range chroma uses its own 224 code-value excursion rather than sample-0.5, bit depth scales footroom and midpoint, and unspecified matrices are inferred by resolution and logged once instead of silently treated as BT.601. Platform/Apple/FfmpegVideoInterop.mm feeds both the CPU converter and the nv12_to_bgra kernel from that one parameter struct, and replaces the bare retained MTLTexture with an owned AppleVideoFrameLease that also retains the CVMetalTexture wrapper and the pixel buffer for as long as the frame can be sampled, with a single release function and an explicit hand-off of a poolable conversion destination; Vulkan/TextureCache holds that lease. New tests: tests/video_decode_pump_test.cpp (13 cases, including reproductions of the previous feed-first order losing a rejected packet and the reordered tail of every loop) and tests/video_color_conversion_test.cpp (9 cases of known pixels, colour bars and range/matrix separation); playback_gpu_test compares the Metal kernel against the CPU reference across both ranges and BT.601/709/2020. P02's first version adds content-rate pacing to the frame clock: FrameTimer takes a pushed FrameDemand whose content_period can only lengthen the tick interval, is ignored below the configured ideal frame time and is clamped to MAX_FRAME_DURATION, so the user's and the display's ceiling always wins and a bad period cannot stall a scene; Scene::single_video_source is set only by CreateVideoProjectScene, beside the construction that justifies it (one video texture, a copy shader, a NoOpShaderValueUpdater, no script, particle, audio or pointer input); VideoTextureSource reports frameDurationSeconds as the shortest plausible period over avg_frame_rate and r_frame_rate so a variable-frame-rate clip cannot lose the frames inside its tightest gap; TextureCache::ShortestVideoFramePeriod returns unknown when any live source cannot answer; and SceneWallpaper pushes the period from the render thread after each frame and on every stop/resume, reporting nothing for any other scene because an authored scene may change on a time uniform, a script write, a particle system, audio reactivity or a feedback texture that is not enumerated. Covered by five new cases in tests/timer/frame_timer_test.cpp, which scripts/check_renderer.py now runs. 2026-09-17 (second round): the scene engine grew renderer work counters (Core/RendererCounters.{h,hpp}, exported through SceneWallpaperBindings as owe_scene_wallpaper_counters / owe_renderer_shared_counters), incremented by the frame clock, the draw handler, the Vulkan submit/present/fence path and the texture cache. Counting is off by default. Video frame pacing moved from container metadata to observed presentation timestamps (Video/VideoFramePacing.{hpp,cpp}), is scaled by playback speed, and can be switched off through MAC_WALLPAPER_ENGINE_DISABLE_CONTENT_PACING for A/B comparison. FrameTimer's suspension threshold now scales with the interval it is pacing at, so a content wait at the pacing clamp is no longer misread as a process suspension. 2026-09-17 (I01): a pure-video wallpaper's media is now decode input rather than a payload. Video/FfmpegVideoTextureSource gained CreateVideoProjectImage, which resolves the manifest entry against the project directory, canonicalises both sides so a symlink is followed before the containment test and anything leaving the project is rejected, and records only the path on the new Image::videoFilePath; SceneWallpaper's CreateVideoProjectScene calls it instead of reading the file into an ImageData buffer. FfmpegVideoTextureSource::Impl opens such a source in place, so the media is neither read into the process nor copied into the shared cache; the in-package case still extracts, but the bytes are staged under a unique name, size-checked and renamed onto the content-addressed name so a concurrent opener cannot see a partial file, and the inline payload is released once the decoder is open. Covered by tests/video_source_input_test.cpp. 2026-09-18 (R02): conversion destinations are pooled against a real byte budget instead of a texture count. Video/VideoConversionBudget.{hpp,cpp} owns the slot sizing, admission, eviction choice and exhaustion policy over opaque handles, so it is tested without a GPU (tests/video_conversion_budget_test.cpp, registered in tests/CMakeLists.txt). Reuse is keyed on the decoded frame's width, height and destination pixel format, never on a display size, and cost comes from MTLTexture.allocatedSize. The ceiling is 256 MiB per pool — one pool per texture cache, that is per renderer instance, so several displays driven by one scene share it — sized as the six destinations that can coexist for one video texture (kMaxImportedVideoFramesPerVideoTex plus kMaxPendingVideoImportSubmissions) at the 3840x2160 reference resolution. That replaces the flat 64 MiB ceiling, which refused any single destination above roughly 4096x4096 and so made a 6K or larger wallpaper allocate and destroy one every generation. Platform/Apple/FfmpegVideoInterop now lends destinations: Take opens a loan, Recycle from the frame lease's deleter is the GPU-completion point that closes it, and a destination still on loan or already pooled is refused rather than handed to a second frame. Vulkan/TextureCache borrows immediately before the import so no loan can be abandoned, ends the loan itself when the import fails, drops pooled shapes the current resolution no longer requests, and reports a destination allocation failure so the same unsatisfiable size is not retried every frame. Exhaustion degrades by stopping caching and logging one line per reason and per partially-hosted shape; Metal's currentAllocatedSize against recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize is the memory-pressure signal, read synchronously with no notification source and no thread. Pool counters (hits, misses, recycles, evictions, refusals, peak resident bytes) are published through VideoTextureSubmissionStats; tests/playback_gpu_test.mm covers a warm 6144x3456 clip reusing one 81 MiB destination and retained frames keeping their destinations out of the pool. 2026-09-18 (third round): ThreadTimer waits to a deadline recomputed on every wake and SetInterval notifies, so a shortened interval no longer sleeps out the previous period; demand-driven video pacing became opt-in through MAC_WALLPAPER_ENGINE_CONTENT_PACING because the period only reaches the clock after a completed frame, which cannot bound frame loss at a rate transition; FfmpegVideoTextureSource carries a process-unique instance id so two decoders on one file are never folded together; and TextureCache publishes that identity next to the decode counters. 2026-09-18 (fourth round): VideoConversionBudget replaced its single pooled-bytes counter with a three-state live ledger — Available (idle in the reuse pool), CheckedOut (handed to an import that has not yet reported the GPU may reference it) and AwaitingGpu (a live imported frame holds it) — whose sum is total_live_conversion_allocation_bytes(), with peak_live_conversion_allocation_bytes() its running maximum. Take now moves bytes between states instead of dropping them, GPU completion removes a handle from the ledger entirely so a re-admission is not billed twice, and Drain, DropOtherKeys, memory pressure and allocation failure still only ever evict Available slots. ReserveAllocation, CommitAllocation and CancelReservation book an allocation before it exists: granted-but-uncommitted estimates stay out of the live total but are charged against the ceiling, and a reservation is never refused for capacity, so a request that still does not fit after the budget sheds its own cache is granted with over_ceiling set and counted in over_ceiling_grants() rather than dropping the decoded frame. Admit gained VideoConversionRefusal::LiveAllocationAtCeiling, but only for speculative caching beyond live demand: admission re-admits bytes that are already live, so refusing it for capacity frees nothing and merely guarantees the caller reallocates the identical destination on the next generation, and the first cached slot of a shape is therefore always accepted however full the ledger is. Only a second or later idle slot of a shape whose in-flight bytes already fill the effective ceiling is refused, and it is refused before anything is evicted so the slot already proven reusable stays cached. VideoConversionMemoryDomain, in the same header/source pair, sums the live totals of the budgets that opt in through AttachDomain and caps them at 512 MiB process-wide; it is mutex-protected, never mutates or frees anything belonging to another budget, and sheds cooperatively, so the budget that shrinks is whichever one next performs an operation. No cross-process coordination with the lock-screen extension exists. The ledger counts reported allocations for conversion destinations only: decode CVPixelBuffers, Vulkan swapchain images and every other intermediate are excluded, and it is not a claim about physical residency. tests/video_conversion_budget_test.cpp covers the state transitions, an in-flight destination surviving every reclamation path, over-ceiling grants and recovery, two budgets competing for one domain's headroom, and a ledger that reads zero once everything is released. Platform/Apple/FfmpegVideoInterop's AppleVideoMetalTexturePool now executes that ledger rather than only its cache: ReserveFresh, CommitFresh and CancelFresh book an allocation before it exists and replace the nominal estimate with MTLTexture.allocatedSize, MarkGpuPending moves a destination from checked out to awaiting GPU once the import succeeded, and CreateAppleVideoFrameLease reports the destination it allocated itself through a borrowed out-parameter, so a freshly created destination is on the books from the moment it exists instead of from the first time it is recycled — the hole that made the reported figure the idle pool alone. Vulkan/TextureCache drives RetainOnly, then Take or ReserveFresh, then the lease, then CommitFresh or CancelFresh, then MarkGpuPending, with Recycle from the lease deleter, and unwinds the ledger on every failure between them. AppleVideoConversionPoolStats and VideoTextureSubmissionStats gained checked_out, awaiting_gpu, live, peak_live, reserved_estimate, over_ceiling_grants and live_slot_count; cached_bytes and peak_cached_bytes keep meaning the Available state alone. The pool opts its budget into SharedVideoConversionMemoryDomain and forgets it on destruction. Core/RendererCounters.h gained OWE_RC_VIDEO_CONVERSION_LIVE_BYTES and OWE_RC_VIDEO_CONVERSION_PEAK_LIVE_BYTES as consumer-work gauges written on the existing import path, with no sampler and no thread, and read only while counting is enabled. Measured in playback_gpu_test for a 6144x3456 clip, where one destination is 84,934,656 bytes: the retired peak_pooled_bytes figure of 84,934,656 covered exactly one idle destination in the reuse pool, while the live peak for the same workload is 339,738,624 bytes — the four destinations the texture cache keeps alive at once, three held by retained imported frames and one checked out to the import in progress. playback_gpu_test emits that ledger as a per-generation trace property and additionally covers a fresh destination being counted before any recycle, and a cleared cache plus destroyed pool leaving every byte counter at zero and the shared domain back at its previous total. A later pass made the per-pool and per-domain books symmetric and the overshoot bounded. Granted-but-uncommitted estimates are now published to VideoConversionMemoryDomain and subtracted from every other budget's headroom, and the fit test and the record of a reservation happen in one locked AcquireHeadroom call, so two pools can no longer be told the same bytes are free; headroom_for stayed a const query that records and counts nothing, with shed requests counted only on the mutating call where the decision is taken. over_ceiling_grants() remained a reason rather than a bound, so ReserveAllocation now refuses with VideoConversionRefusal::InFlightCapReached when the caller already holds kCoexistingSlots destinations in flight — the quantity capped is loan_count(), never live_slot_count(), because a cached slot has already been returned and is what the next import reuses. That refusal is reported once per episode, recovers as soon as a destination is returned, and bounds the excess over the ceiling at kCoexistingSlots destinations of the requested shape instead of merely counting it. 2026-09-18: trimmed to what this repository builds — removed the waywallen host (waywallen/), Qt QML helper (qml_helper/), standalone viewer (standalone_view/), README, FUNDING workflow and stale .gitmodules, plus their BUILD_WAYWALLEN/BUILD_QML CMake options and presets; third_party/miniaudio keeps only miniaudio.h, LICENSE and README (extras, examples, tests, website, research, resources, tools and change log removed); third_party/spirv_reflect keeps the library sources, LICENSE and README (tests, examples and its vendored googletest removed; the build never enabled them). wpdoc/ and tests/ are retained. Restore removed files from the pinned revision if needed. 2026-09-18: internal render scale and shared video decode land in the scene engine; see the renderer note for the full list of touched files. 2026-09-19 (round 8, native Metal backend second version): SceneRendererHandle starts with no backend and gains createVulkan/createMetal/release/hasBackend plus a ServicePosterRequest forwarder; SceneWallpaper.cpp creates the GPU backend in selectSceneBackend() after the scene is parsed instead of at INIT_VULKAN (offscreen and layer-less surfaces still create Vulkan at init), gates LOAD_SCENE on the surface description rather than an inited renderer, adds CMD_POSTER_REQUEST and falls back to the compatibility backend when a native drawFrame fails; RenderInitInfo gains bind_poster_wake and SceneBackendSelection gains `created` so owe_scene_wallpaper_backend() reports -1 until a backend exists; SceneWallpaperBindings.mm guards DesktopPosterMailbox with a mutex and credits deliveries to the request id in flight when the capture started. New Scene/MetalRender sources: MetalPosterCapture.{hpp,mm} (on-request final-composition readback), MetalVideoTextures.{hpp,mm} (BGRA zero-copy import and NV12 compute conversion encoded into the frame's command buffer) and MetalVideoSupport.{hpp,cpp}; MetalRender.{hpp,mm}, MetalCapability.cpp and ScenePassDescription.{hpp,cpp} now lower and execute effect chains, post-process passes, link textures, break copies, resampling copies and mip generation, with history feedback, depth and MSAA targets still rejected. Platform/Apple/FfmpegVideoInterop gains the additive AppleVideoFrameColorParams. wpMetalRender links CoreVideo. New tests metal_poster_capture_test.mm and metal_video_texture_test.mm; metal_backend_test.cpp and metal_scene_draw_smoke.mm extended. 2026-09-19 (round 9, scene optimisation on Metal, sprite sheets and 2D sprite particles): Scene/MetalRender/MetalRender.mm reuses wpVulkanRender's StaticSubgraphCache and PlanCopyElision over its own lowered pass list -- per-target reuse with a per-frame sample that folds node transform, mesh revision, material constants, the pass camera's and the active camera's view-projection, the sprite frame rectangle and the target extent; copies are elided as dead or aliased, an aliased destination shares its source's MTLTexture instead of getting one, and pinned bytes and skipped/elided counts go into the existing process-wide totals. resolveTexture imports every image slot so a sheet's imageId selects one, prepareDraw fills the pass sprite map, and dynamic meshes get per-in-flight-frame vertex and index storage sized at the mesh's capacity with a per-slot uploaded-revision check. MetalCapability drops the blanket particle-emitter and sprite-sheet refusals and decides per mesh instead: rope, trail and every other per-frame geometry still fall back whole-scene. SpriteAnimation.hpp gains FrameAt/CurFrameIndex; SpecTexs.hpp gains WE_PRENDER_SPRITE and WE_PRENDER_TRAIL, set by WPSceneParser next to the particle mesh they describe. Defect found while porting and fixed in BOTH backends: a read of a copy destination the plan aliased away resolved to a name no pass writes, so the reader looked dependency-free and could be cached while its real source was redrawn every frame -- CopyElision gains ResolveCopyAliasKey and VulkanRender.cpp resolves inputs through it. Second fix in both: planStaticSkips now drops the cached verdicts while the setting is off, so turning it back on cannot reuse a target whose recorded signature predates the frames drawn while it was off. Tests: metal_backend_test.cpp, metal_scene_draw_smoke.mm and static_subgraph_cache_test.cpp extended.
